Subject: sudden 5xx spike + request for executive attention

Hi Laura,

We started seeing a sustained increase in 5xx errors and tail latency for our endpoint (embed-v2) at ~08:50 PDT. Error rate has climbed to ~7% over the last 20 minutes; p95 latency jumped from 180ms to ~1.8s. This is impacting our checkout flow and several streaming features.

Attached are a few sample traces and a short log snippet. Our engineering team is already collecting traces but we need help on:
- immediate mitigation to reduce customer-facing errors
- ETA on throughput capacity increase or recommended fallback model
- an exec-level liaison for communications to our leadership (CTO + Ops).

Can you confirm receipt and next steps? We're standing by for a bridge.

Thanks,
Alice Zhang
Head of Platform, Marigold AI

On bridge now — quick notes from triage:
- Error taxonomy: ~65% are 5xx with 'KV cache miss + OOM-retry' trace pattern; remaining are upstream 504s from customer origin.
- Observed a sudden burst from a small subset of API keys with large batch sizes (~10k tokens) — seems correlated.
- Karthik: initial hypothesis is a combination of very large sequence lengths and a fallback path that doesn’t handle prefix caching correctly.

Actionables assigned:
- Karthik: hotfix to adjust KV cache eviction threshold + guardrails for requests >4k tokens (ETA 45m).
- Aditya: activate burst GPU pool (reserved capacity) for Marigold account and temporarily lower batch-size threshold at the routing layer (ETA 20m).
- Grace: prepare an executive-facing status (one paragraph + bulleted next steps).

I’ll coordinate a short customer update once we have the hotfix and evidence of a declining error rate.

Marissa
Senior Director, Customer Ops
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 09:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden 5xx spike + request for executive attention

Update from runtime: implemented a conservative hotfix to KV eviction (non-disruptive) and added a per-customer max-token guard at the routing layer. Rolling to Marigold shard now (10% -> 50% -> 100%) — current rollout at 40%. Early telemetry: 5xx rate down to 2.1% on the canary subset; p95 latency down ~40% there.

Notes:
- The hotfix prevents the fallback code-path from repeatedly attempting a large-KV restore under load. It's a short-term patch; we will follow up with a targeted patch to optimize the restore routine.
- Aditya: if you can confirm burst GPU pool activation and no queueing backlog, we can accelerate the rollout.

Karthik
Lead, Serving Runtime
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Alice Zhang <alice@marigold.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <cto@marigold.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Marigold status update — remediation progress and next steps

Alice / Ethan — quick executive summary and customer-facing status for your leadership:

Summary (current):
- Incident: elevated 5xx error-rate and tail latency affecting embed-v2 endpoints. Root cause (interim): large sequence-length requests triggering a KV-cache restore loop under constrained serving conditions.
- Impact: temporary increase in failed/slow requests for a subset of high-volume keys; customer checkout degradation reported.
- Remediation in progress: hotfix to KV eviction & per-request guard deployed progressively; canary telemetry shows 5xx down from ~7% to ~2% and p95 improved roughly 40% on canary traffic.

Actions taken:
- We activated Marigold’s burst GPU pool and lowered batch-size at routing to reduce concurrent KV pressure.
- Karthik’s runtime patch shipped as a short-term fix; a follow-up code change to optimize restore performance is scheduled for this week.
- We are prepping a post-incident runbook with root-cause analysis and regression tests; expected delivery within 5 business days.

Customer-facing asks & timeline:
- Short note you can forward to your execs: "Redwood has taken immediate mitigations, and preliminary telemetry indicates error rates are decreasing. We have activated additional capacity and deployed a runtime mitigation; Redwood will provide a full RCA and remediation plan within 5 business days."
- ETA for full remediation: preliminary patch and testing complete by 2028-05-27; a permanent performance improvement release targeted the week starting 2028-06-04.

Compensation/credits: I’ve requested a discretionary credit while we stabilize — I will confirm details once legal approves (ETA same-day).

Bridge & follow-ups: ongoing bridge here: https://console.redwood.ai/bridges/BR-9982. If you prefer a short exec-to-exec call, I am available at 09:30 PDT today.

We’ll continue to post updates. Please reply if you need tighter SLAs or immediate escalations.

—Laura
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
